utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, Daryl Mundis, and Andres Vatter, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Edina Residovic, counsel, Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel, and Mirna Milanovic, legal assistant, representing General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant, on behalf of Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber would like to greet everybody present in the courtroom, especially the new Madam Registrar who is here temporarily with us. I would like to welcome everybody else in the courtroom, representatives of the OTP, the Defence counsel, the accused, as well as the interpreters in their booths. According to our schedule, we should be finished with this witness today. I hope, sir, that you had a good weekend. Unfortunately, although your testimony was supposed to be finished last Friday, it had to be continued today. I know that the Defence wanted the floor, and that's why I'm turning towards the Defence counsel and I am giving them the floor. Maybe it's going to be Mr. Bourgon who wants to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we just wanted to inform you that in keeping with your decision, the witness has marked the map again in the presence of the registry and the interpreters. In view of the fact that the map will still be continued, we would like the witness to sign the map, and we will tender this map into evidence. We also wanted to inform you, Mr. President, that we are still awaiting your decision with regard to the expert historian so as enable us to inform this expert when he's supposed to arrive. He is a full-time professor at a university, so he needs to be informed. The only thing that we emphasised with regard to the witnesses for the next three weeks is the fact that the schedule may be changed in case one or the other witness cannot obtain their passports in due course. At noon today, we were informed that the witnesses which were scheduled to follow the expert Cehic are supposed to obtain their passports tomorrow. Should this not be the case, we are going to inform the Trial Chamber about the change of the order in the scheduling of the witnesses. So some of the witnesses which were scheduled for later would replace the first two witnesses. The only thing that we are certain of is that Dr. Menzel is not going to be able to obtain his passport because he was not able to obtain the necessary documents. Instead of Dr. Menzel, we are going to call Sead Jusic. We will have full information tomorrow, and we will advise the Trial Chamber and our learned friends from the OTP accordingly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Residovic. As far as the expert is concerned, expert who is supposed to arrive on Monday, the 1st of November, the written decision was rendered this morning, and it's going to certainly be delivered to the Registry. So in accordance with this decision, we're awaiting this expert witness. You're going to have an hour and a half for your examination-in-chief, and the Prosecution is going to have an hour and a half for their cross-examination. As far as the other difficulties are concerned, we hope that they will be resolved in due course. As you have already informed us, on Friday, the 29th, nothing has been scheduled. So maybe on Friday either in the morning or in the afternoon, in keeping with the availability of the courtrooms, maybe you can have some of the witnesses arrive on that day. According to the schedule for Thursday, Friday, if all the witnesses arrive as scheduled, maybe there won't be a need to have a session on Friday. Today, Mr. -- the witness is supposed to finish. We have only one witness that is supposed to follow on Wednesday. Another witness that is scheduled, and on Thursday we have the next witness. For the moment, nobody's scheduled for Friday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Since we were informed that on Friday will be regular court maintenance and therefore the courtrooms won't be available, that is why we have cancelled a witness that was scheduled for this week. So bringing a new witness in lieu of that one would pose some difficulties to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Sir, I hope that you had a good rest. I understand that you marked the map in the presence of the OTP, the Registry, and the interpreter. Your testimony is going to continue with the questions put to you by the Prosecution. And after that, you will be examined by the Judges. Mrs. Benjamin or Mr. Mundis, I don't know who is going to lead this witness. Mrs. Benjamin, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: When we broke on Friday, I was just beginning the cross-examination about your role as chief of staff. I would just like us to clarify a few points before we move on. Firstly, could you tell me -- could you relate for the Trial Chamber, the hierarchy, how it operated. Who was first? Was it the commander first? Who was at the top?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade commander was at the head of the brigade. And there is a chief of staff, his assistants for security, the assistant for moral guidance and religious affairs, the assistant for logistics, the assistant for financial matters and business matters are attached to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. And that is with respect to the brigade. Now, I'm talking about the 3rd Corps as a whole. The first senior position in the 3rd Corps, would it be the commander?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the brigade. However, I was supposed to know, and I knew, that a commander was at the head of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And below the commander would be the chief of staff. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of staff in the brigade was also the deputy commander of the brigade on such occasions when the commander was absent from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would I be correct in saying that the chief of staff was responsible for disseminating orders given by the commander?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm this statement fully because the chief of staff was responsible for disseminating orders of the commander which were relative to the officers who were in the brigade staff. And the assistant commanders for logistics, security, and moral guidance and other assistants were in direct communication with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now, if I were to ask you who were you subordinated to, who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very simple. The commander was my superior, and I reported directly to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And your subordinates would have been who? Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to my subordinates, I can tell you. But I got a wrong interpretation. Are you referring to those that reported to me directly?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the staff, the chief of staff had his assistants. So the -- his immediate subordinates were the assistant chief of staff for operations and education, who was also the deputy chief of staff. At the beginning in the staff, there was also the assistant for organisation and mobilisation, the assistant chief of staff for intelligence, the chief of communications, the chief of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But overall, you would have been superior to all these people? You were in charge of all of these people?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And similarly, the commander is in charge of everyone?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military hierarchy of the former JNA and the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the commander was superior to the entire command, to all those persons who were members of the command and his command function was exercised via his assistants in the brigade command or in some other command.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So as you quite rightly said in response to my learned friend on the 22nd, the commander is the commander of everyone. The commander holds responsibility for all in the army.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand your question fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I asked you a while ago who were your subordinates, and you illustrated a few positions. And then you said you were superior to all of these people. Then I asked you who was your superior, and you said the commander. So I'm saying to you now, and correct me if I'm wrong or if you agree with me, please say so, but the commander is responsible for everyone per se?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. The commander is responsible for the entire unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you, in fact, qualified that to my learned friend. You said that the commander is responsible for everyone. In your position as chief of staff -- in your position as chief of staff, you would have to relate --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe -- there is either a mistake in what I heard or what I can read in line 7. As far as I understood, in line 7, 8, the witness answered properly that the commander is responsible for the entire unit. My learned friend in 710 does not mention the entire unit. She alleged that he said that he was responsible for everybody. This is not precise because this does not reflect what the witness has just said before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: With all due respect, I think the witness understood because he does answer in line 8. He says the commander is responsible for the entire unit. So he did understand what I said to him: Is the commander responsible for everyone per se from chief of staff, right down.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the subordinates in his unit, for all the subordinates in his unit. I'm not talking about anybody outside the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: We can only talk about the unit that he's in control of. And we're talking now about the 3rd Corps, the commander of the 3rd Corps. Who was he responsible for?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to be aware of the entire situation. However, looking at the entire hierarchy and the principles of the use of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the corps commander, and this is only my opinion, was responsible for all the subordinate commands, units, and staffs within the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could you give us an idea of the size of the 306th Mountain Brigade. Can you give us an idea of how many soldiers were in your brigade.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the period. The 306th Brigade had a different number of troops and different quantity of equipment. The 306th Brigade was supposed to be a mountain brigade with four battalions and the other units attached to the staff. However, this brigade was never replenished to the full as far as the troops are concerned. And as far as the equipment is concerned, the situation was even worse. Before the conflict, on the eve of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, at this time could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P239, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And I wish to draw your attention to B.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see very well what it says here. The 312th Brigade under item C was supposed to be a motorised brigade. And according to its formation, it was supposed to have 4.000 troops. The 306th Brigade, according to the formation, was a mountain brigade, and I suppose that the person who drafted this document, this information did not have enough information or the information was incomplete when it came to replenishment of these two units.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I am particularly dealing with B, not C, for the moment. We're just dealing with B. And is it your evidence that this is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: What about paragraph 1, line 4. Is this also incorrect?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just give me a moment to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that I had, I knew how many troops the 306th Brigade had at that time. At that time, the Frankopan Brigade had still not been established. Only the Travnik Brigade had been established from the HVO troops. And I can speak based on that. I don't know how many troops the other BiH army units in Travnik had. According to my estimate, as I speak here today, I could say that this information is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would you be able to say, then, whether the 306th Brigade was a larger army than the army that operated in that area for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that at that moment and at that time, there were still no conflicts. The number of troops in the 306th Brigade, there were more troops than members of the HVO in the area from which the 306th Brigade was replenished. And here, look at this item where it says that the officer for exchange also mentions the 306th Brigade located in Mali Mosunj. Mali Mosunj is a village, a completely Croatian village, and it is surrounded by Croats. And not for a single moment could one unit enter a village, let alone be deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But if you want to look at it, too, look at B now. And he specifies a particular figure, three to four thousand, and he specifies where it was reporting from, from Krajina. And is it your evidence still that that is incorrect at that time? January 1993.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was talking about the 306th Brigade, I said that there was an order which regulated the establishment of the 306th Brigade from the troops of the Biljanska valley, the detachments which had existed in the area of the Biljanska valley. One of such detachments or battalions had existed, and its name was the Siprage Battalion. On its strength, it had some hundred troops who were armed. So it was not a battalion. There was a tendency, however, that this should develop into a battalion. It was replenished from the sector of Kotor Varos Municipality and Siprage village, from the territory of the population that had been expelled from Skender Vakuf and Mrkonjic Grad. The total number of such groups from this area which we do not call Krajina, for us Krajina extends from Sanski Most to Bihac, this is what we call Bosanska Krajina. And this area closer from which this battalion was replenished was almost next to Travnik Municipality, and there could not have been than a battalion of them. And the 4th Brigade, according to the list, never had more than 2.400 people, according to the list of troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay, let's for argument --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise for the interruption. I believe that there has been a mistake in the interpretation, page 10, line 9. It says that the 306th Brigade was Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond replenished from the troops in the Biljanska valley. The witness said from the people, from the population in the Biljanska valley. Can this be taken into consideration, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And I would make it simple for you and for everybody else. For argument's sake, let's say this document is wrong. You tell the Trial Chamber in your opinion which was the stronger army in Travnik at the time, prior to the conflict in January and during the conflict? Which in your opinion was the stronger army?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you please repeat your answer since we weren't receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was saying that I was more familiar with the situation in the Bila valley because I was a member of the 306th Brigade. And to the extent that I was familiar with the situation in Travnik, and if you only evaluate the strength on the basis of number of men, in such a case you could draw the conclusion that the BH Republic Army was stronger in terms of manpower. So it was stronger in that sense. However, if you take into account the equipment that the HVO had at its disposal, then the relationship, the balance of force, is quite different.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And if you were to give us an estimate in figures so we could balance this thing for ourselves, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Travnik Municipality formed two brigades, the 312th and the 306th. At that time, the HVO had one brigade, the HVO Travnik Brigade. And it had formed some sort of reserve battalion. I don't know what it was called exactly. And if we only took manpower into consideration, then naturally -- well, I don't know how many men the 312th had. But according to what I heard, the 312th Brigade never had over 3.000 men. So there were 2.000 in the 306th. I'm just taking into account there. And the TO municipal staff in Travnik never managed to form detachments which were regulated by orders. So in the municipal staff, there was an insignificant number of men. And if you put this into relation with a brigade, then one could say that there were -- the ratio was 5.000 to 2.000 or 2.500. And that concerns the number of men in units. In terms of men, in terms of manpower, the BH Army was twice as strong.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to the foreigners, as we call them, and I deal particularly now with the mujahedin, not the journalists, not the other foreigners, specifically the mujahedin, would you be able to tell us where they were based first?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, at the beginning, I don't know exactly when, it was either late summer or the beginning of autumn, at that time, I saw these people moving around town. And later on, when visiting the Mehurici Detachment which was part of the municipal defence staff in Travnik, I found out from the commander of the detachment that some of the mujahedin were located in the Mehurici school on the floor. The commander of the detachment of -- the Territorial Defence in Mehurici was located in the premises, just the command. And that's where they were on duty, where they maintained channels of communication. And the mujahedin were located on the floor in that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So if I have understood you correct, perhaps the 1st Battalion command was located in the Mehurici school on one floor, and the mujahedin were in that very school on other floor?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You have misunderstood me. I said that when I worked in the TO staff in Travnik Municipality, at that time there was a Mehurici Detachment. There were no brigades. This was in 1992, in autumn. And I was saying that the command of that detachment, not the command of the 1st Battalion, the command of that detachment was located there. It was perhaps in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Do you know if any other brigade from the 3rd Corps was located in the Mehurici school? Do you know if there was any other?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, when brigades first started functioning, well, I have to talk about the existence of detachments before the formation of brigades. I was talking about the period before the formation of the brigades --

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you. Can I interrupt you. I don't think we need to go that far. Let me just cast your mind back to something that you said to my learned friend on the 21st. And she says to you, and she was speaking in particular to the problems that you said you were having with the mujahedin, and this is what she says: "As to other problems, as far as other problems were concerned, where were your men located? The 306th have the facilities for billeting these men in listed barracks [sic]." Now, here we go, here's your answer: "The 306th Brigade -- well, first of all I could talk about the commands. They didn't have any facilities for accommodating the commands, but they found facilities in the premises of the Bila mine. We didn't have any barracks anywhere but the commands of the battalions usually use schools as premises --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: "The schools that were in the area. So the 1st Battalion command was located in the school in Mehurici."

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. I can confirm that. But when you asked me a question a minute ago, I thought you were asking me about where the mujahedin were when I first saw them. And I'm telling you that before the 306th Brigade was formed, I saw them for the first time in October 1992 when I was visiting the commander of the detachment. But as far as the 306th Brigade is concerned, the commander of the 1st Battalion was there. It wanted to locate itself in the school with the men. They had nowhere to sleep. There were a lot of refugees. So at that point in time, the mujahedin had to move out of that school, but they kept two to three offices on the first floor of that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So my question to you, then, was: One battalion operated one floor of the Mehurici school. Am I correct? The mujahedins operated another floor in the Mehurici school. Am I correct? And I speak of the base you indicated to us. I'm not speaking previously when you first found them. I speak of where they were based, we just want to deal with where they were based at this point. Now, according to you, they were based in the Mehurici school. And I'm trying to establish the positions, the mujahedins were based there, the command was based there. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there is a misunderstanding as a result of the interpretation, or perhaps I'm not being sufficiently clear. I said that in the basement of the school, there were several premises, and that's where the command of the 1st Battalion was located with some of the men who didn't have any houses. The classrooms were used as a barracks and as a home. And on the first floor, the mujahedin kept two to three offices, and they left their materiel and equipment there. But they themselves had already moved to Poljanica where they would spend a fairly lengthy period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now, I think you sort of understand what I'm trying to achieve, and that is that the presence of the mujahedins was there along with the presence of people from the 1st Battalion command. Whether or not they were there for a while and then they moved, or whether they moved and just left offices. The presence of the mujahedin, along with the presence of the 1st Battalion. Some were in the basement as you said; some were on another floor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, men from the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade were in the basement. There were offices used by the mujahedin on the first floor. But they themselves weren't there. They would just appear occasionally to take their possessions. That's the information I received when I visited my subordinate units and commands. This is the information Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond that they provided me with.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So this is my question to you, then: You had no connection whatsoever with the mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, we didn't have any connection with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: At the time and after the time, did you at any time at all have any connection with the mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I had some sort of connection with them, the first time there were official documents or connections with the mujahedin was at the end of August 1993. From the 3rd Corps command, we received an order according to which -- an order to carry out combat operations, the El Mujahid detachment would be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. I can't remember the exact date; I think it was towards the end of August. But in order to implement this resubordination and plan combat operations, the command of the 306th Brigade tried to establish contact with the command of the El Mujahid Detachment. The command of the El Mujahid Detachment at that time did not agree to being resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. And as far as that order on the resubordination of the El Mujahid -- of the resubordination of the El Mujahid detachment to the 306th was concerned, it was never implemented. This order was never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would you be able to assist the Trial Chamber with the numbers of mujahedins. Could you tell us about how much made up this group? Would you be able to assist us with that?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Haven't I been sufficiently clear? We weren't able to establish contact with them, or rather they didn't want to be resubordinated. So at that time, and I'll repeat this: At the end of August 1993, we did not establish contact with them. Later on, perhaps later when I wasn't in the 306th Brigade, we may have been involved in certain activities that had to do with the El Mujahid Detachment or linked to that detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: A while ago you said to us that they had left the Mehurici school and took up quarters in Poljanica, am I right? Not far from Mehurici. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can. I said that the 306th or the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade used the basement of the school to billet the battalion, to locate the commander of the battalion and its men there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Not so far back. I said to you, and this is what I said to you: That you had indicated to us that the mujahedins had left the Mehurici school and had taken up quarters in Poljanica, which is not far from Mehurici. And I was asking you if I was correct.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that they held on to two to three offices on the first floor in order to keep their materiel and equipment there. And occasionally, they would go to these offices of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And it is your evidence that even when they were in the Poljanica area, that you had absolutely nothing to do with the mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, we didn't have anything to do with them. On the basis of the information I had at my disposal, no, we had nothing to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you at any time feel that the mujahedins were a source of embarrassment to the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So far, in the course of my testimony, I have said that mujahedin represented a certain problem for the entire population. As far as I am concerned, I can tell you about a problem because my wife had a problem with the mujahedin. My wife is a teacher. And in 1993, in a village in which I was a born, she taught children. Followers of those mujahedin arrived in my village, and they drove my wife away from the village because her name is Snjezana. My wife comes from a mixed marriage; her father is a Muslim and her mother a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sir, I sympathise. But I need to clarify this: And I will refer you to a question that my learned friend asked you on Friday. And it said: "Did you know or did the brigade command know who they are" - refer to the mujahedins - "what their names were? Did you have any precise information that would enable you to report in detail to your superior command"? And your response was: "I am not sure that anyone at any time had precise information about them" - referring to the mujahedins - "and to tell you the truth, we were not even interested. They were not within our field of competence. We did not seek information about them. We did not know who they were or who their commanders were. They were not strictly established as a combat group. And to me, they were some sort of passersby that I avoided because all I could expect from them was inconvenience and embarrassment." And my question to you now, why, if you had absolutely nothing to do with the mujahedins, why would they be a source of embarrassment to you? When I say "to you," I mean to the 306th.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say a source of embarrassment, as far as the 306th is concerned and the civilian population, I could provide you with numerous examples of mujahedin approaching women who didn't have veils on them and who weren't behaving in accordance with Islam regulations such as they were interpreted by the mujahedin. Furthermore, they would appear in cafes, break things up, open fire in cafes. They wanted absolute power. They wanted to be in control of everything, and they wanted everything to be done in accordance with their ideas. They tried to establish certain standards of behaviour. Members of the 306th Brigade were maltreated as well, and this is why I said that we avoided them, and they were only a source of embarrassment for members of the 306th Brigade and for the civilian population who weren't respecting their rules and regulations, who weren't behaving in accordance with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And that is precisely why I asked the question, because to me, sir, the mujahedins could only be a source of embarrassment to you because you represented them in some particular way, and that is why on account of their behaviour you were embarrassed.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, there is a document that I would like to show the witness. It is not a Prosecution exhibit, but it has been disclosed to the Defence, and I just wish to show the witness. I have provided my learned friends with a copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sir, I do not want you to read the whole document because I don't think we have enough time for that. But I want you to tell me who signed this document, if you can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us which document we provided you with so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: It's 01855653, the one that we said was just disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a document, and the end of the number is 652. 652.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: 652, 653, 655 in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I thought that my learned colleague was saying that this was a document that we had given to the Prosecution. However, we received this document from the Prosecution on Friday. And in accordance with the practice today, this document should also be provided to the accused so that everyone can follow. This is an entirely new document provided by the Prosecution. It was provided on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Do you have two copies for the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the Prosecution tell us what the relevance of this document is? Because in relation to General Enver Hadzihasanovic, as far as I can see, this does not pertain to the charges leveled against him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could you tell the Chamber Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond where this document comes from, from which archives, how did you obtain it. And secondly, as far as its relevance is concerned, could you inform us of the relevance of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think at this stage it would be advisable if we take the witness out of the room, please, so that we can give a thorough explanation as to the source of the document, when it was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Benjamin, we are in open session. Can you please tell us about the origin of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document comes out of the ABiH archives. It was disclosed to the Defence in January 2002. And it comes out of the compilation of the seven CDs. It's included -- that document is included in the seven CDs. In addition to that, the Defence was served with the documents since Friday. And as to relevance, I think my friend just has to look at column 1, and she will be able to see exactly where -- or follow the trend of what is taking place. My friend quite rightly put to the witness on Friday that they had no control over the mujahedins, they didn't know anything about the mujahedins, the mujahedins had no business with them. And this document surely says something else or speaks to something else. And it is an order that is done by this very witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, yes, there is his signature on page 3. Very well, then. Let me summarise. The Prosecution tells us that this document is relevant. It is relevant because in one of the columns, there is a reference to the 306th Brigade. It was signed by the witness, and it is -- it refers to the question of the mujahedin because in line 4, we have it here. The commander of El Mujahid is mentioned in line 4. So this document should have been sent to the mujahedin unit. What does the Defence have to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first I would like to repeat my procedural objection. This document should have been on the OTP list of additional documents, and for any other document that they wish to tender, that the OTP would have to seek permission from the Trial Chamber. As for the relevance, it is correct that I asked the witness to tell me whether the 306th Brigade ever had any connection or subordination or connection with the mujahedins. And the witness responded that the 306th never had the role of superiority over the mujahedins. I am claiming that this document is not relevant because General Hadzihasanovic left the duty of the corps commander on the 1st of November 1993. Then it is clear from the document that this document was drafted in December 1993. Secondly, the witness said that while he was in the 306th Brigade, he never had any contact with the mujahedin, and the signature that we see on this document speaks of the chief of staff of the operations group, Bosanska Krajina, during the time when this witness had a completely different position in the BH Army. For that reason, this document does not have any relevance, and it shouldn't be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, the establishment of the mujahedin unit that are mentioned in the document, this unit was established in August 1993. So during the period of when the -- he was the commander of the 3rd Corps because he asked for the integration of that unit into Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it was established in August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Mr. President. And you have heard the witness, General Garrod and General Williams, who testified, and there are also documents testifying to the meeting between General Garrod and General Hadzihasanovic. The commander of the 3rd Corps and the 3rd Corps itself attempted to place the El Mujahid unit on their control. The witnesses that I've just mentioned testified before this Trial Chamber that this happened when the corps commander was General Alagic. There's a difference between the two issues. One issue is the issuance of an order, and the second issue is the effective control of that unit while General Hadzihasanovic was the commander of the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let me summarise. The Prosecution would like to put some questions to the witness with regard to the fact whether the 306th Brigade had any relations with the mujahedin or the El Mujahid unit. With regard to the question put by the Prosecution, the witness responded no, save for the fact they were in the Mehurici school. But apart from that, we didn't have any connection with them. The Prosecution now would like to show the document to the witness in order to ask the witness for his point of view and to ask the witness whether he could confirm whether there was a problem. Or we have a problem here. Either the witness lies or he did not have any relation with the mujahedins and El Mujahid unit. And if that is the case, how could he draft this document in which the commander of the El Mujahid unit is mentioned? In any case, this witness should be able to clarify this. As far as the questions are concerned and the time reference, and the time scale, the two accused were not members of the 3rd Corps because they left the 1st of November. General Alagic left. So he was no longer the commander of the 3rd Corps. But we shouldn't forget that this unit was established in August, and that it was functioning in August, September, and October. So during the three months when he was in command of the 3rd Corps. We should ask the witness to give us his explanation about the paragraph 4 on page 1. Can you please fetch the witness, Mr. Usher, because it is already half past 3.00. Ms. Benjamin, you may put your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sir, first I would like you to indicate to the Trial Chamber whose signature is that at the back of the document. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And then I would like you to turn to the front of the document. It says "order number," "number 1." "Contents of work." And if you can read the first paragraph under 1 for us, and could you explain to us what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under item 1, it says: "Hold a meeting with commanders of the units taking part in the operation. The 17th Glorious Krajina Mountain Brigade, the 27th, the 306th, 308th, 312th, 325th Mountain Brigade, the El Mujahid Detachment, and Manoeuvre."

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what was your reason for writing this and what's this all about, please.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the Honourable Chamber is aware of the fact that during all this time of conflict between the BH Army and the HVO, in Stari Vitez, there was an area of 500 by 1.000 metres where a Muslim minority was encircled. And this was part of the plan for the operation to rescue these people who were encircled. So this is just one of the documents testifying to the preparations of the BH Army in December 1993 to help the encircled population which cried for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So then, sir, what you would have said to us previously would be inconsistent to this. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to look at the transcript again, and you will see that I said that the first time I saw a written document about the El Mujahid Detachment was towards the end of August. This is not the first document where the El Mujahid Detachment is mentioned. And I even said that this may even originate from a later period when I was no longer on duty in the 306th Brigade. I did not say that I never cooperated, that we never had contacts with the El Mujahid Detachment, but during that period we did not have contacts between them and the 306th Brigade. The first contact between the 306th Brigade and the El Mujahid Detachment was toward the end of August when we received an order for the resubordination of the El Mujahid Detachment for some operations. We received that order from the corps command, and the El Mujahid Detachment did not want to be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. But this dates from a later period. This document dates from a later period.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: When you gave your evidence on Friday in chief, and correct me if Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond I'm wrong, the impression that the Prosecution got, and I think the impression that the Court may have gotten, is that you had absolutely nothing to do with the mujahedins. They were a source of embarrassment. In fact, you said you thought it was out of your competence --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, firstly, I believe that it is up to the Trial Chamber to receive information and to interpret the witness's answers. But I believe that it is my right to ask my learned friend not to paraphrase, but to quote the transcript. So if she wants to quote the transcript, she can do that, but I don't think she should be allowed to paraphrase the witness's words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Benjamin, the Defence would like you to quote the witness, mentioning the page of the transcript where the witness said something. Where is it that he said that he never had any contacts with the El Mujahid unit or the mujahedin themselves? You have 25 minutes to do that, to locate the page, because it is the time for a break. We shall resume at 4.00. At 4.00, the Prosecution will give us the exact number of page and the place where the witness stated that he never had any contacts with the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Much obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Benjamin, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, at the break -- before the break, I think the Defence wanted us to actually quote the paragraphs rather than paraphrase in the interests of time. So I would have to go through different paragraphs. One was the -- the first paragraph was one that we already dealt with, and it was page 41, lines 8 to 14 on day 22. Day 22, page 41, lines 8 to 14. And I don't know if my friend wants me to read out all, but I can. "I'm not sure that any one at any time had precise information about them, and to tell you the truth, we were not even interested. They were not within our field of competence. We did not seek information about them."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: "We didn't know who they were or who their commanders were. They were not strictly established as a combat group. To me, they were some sort of passersby that I avoided because all I could expect from them was inconvenience and embarrassment." The second one would have been page 34 and 35, day 22. And at the bottom of page 34, lines 21, in answer to a question, he says: "I cannot tell you they are the same persons but they are from the same group because there were frequent movements of this group. And at a distance, I did not recognise them." Page 35: "Neither then or the entire duration of my stay with the 306th Brigade did our brigade have a superior position to the mujahedins. We had no control over them." Page 54, lines 8 and 9: "I believe that in my earlier testimony, I have noted several times that we had no such authority. We never did or even attempted to."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. You may put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, before the break and before the interruption, I want to ask you, please, if you could explain to us exactly what column 1, the first one entailed, what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you will allow me just a few words of explanation with regard to the transcript passages that have just been read out. Whatever I said then was relative to the period when the El Mujahid Detachment was still not established as a unit. What I was saying about the mujahedin is relative to the period up to the establishment of the El Mujahid Detachment. Towards the end of August, the 306th Brigade received an order to place the El Mujahid Detachment to their command in order to carry out an action. I never said that during my tour of duty or during my position as an officer of the BiH Army, I never had contacts with the El Mujahid Detachment. I was referring to the mujahedins who were an informal group and who were never in practical terms resubordinated to the 306th Brigade while I was its member. And as far as the question is concerned, the column 1 represents the contents of the work relative to the preparation for the operation to help the Bosniaks encircled in Stari Vitez. Under number 1 here, a meeting should have been held with the commanders of the units which were supposed to participate in this operation. This is the plan of preparations for the operation. The entire document is the plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And according to your statement, the El Mujahid would have been one of the units which were supposed to participate in the operation. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now, I noticed on page 28 of the transcript, line 16, if you could still see it on your screen, your response was "I was referring to the mujahedins who were an informal group and who were never in practical terms resubordinated to the 306th Brigade while I was a member." Now "resubordinated" tells me they were subordinated before.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. In the military terminology, if somebody is subordinated, that means that that group is a member of that unit. Resubordinated means that its command attaches a certain group for a period of time in order to carry out a task. On a number of occasions, I have mentioned the units which were subordinated to the 306th Brigade. Those were the units which were on its strength. The mujahedins were never either subordinated or resubordinated to the 306th, I believe. The resubordination which was ordered at the end of August was never executed, and the El Mujahid Detachment never accepted to be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask you a linguistical question. In English there is the word subordinated and resubordinated. You are saying that these terms should be understood as subordinated and attached to or resubordinated. Can you please explain what distinction do you make in military terms between subordinated and attached to or resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every unit has its prescribed formation or establishment which regulates the number of command staff, the number of units, their strength, and the troops. According to that establishment, the resubordinated units are those which are attached to a different unit from a different command, and their attachment or subordination is of a limited period just for the execution of a certain task.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Page 29, line 14, "the resubordinate which was ordered at the end of August was never executed, and the El Mujahid Detachment never accepted to be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade." That's what you just told us.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And that's -- look at the date of the document you have before you.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp tells me that it was processed on the 7th of December 1993. That is when it was entered into files.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes. And higher up opposite to the one, "time from/to," 712/712. Now, if I were to follow you, according to you, the resubordinate which was ordered at the end of August was never executed, and the El Mujahid Detachment never accepted to be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. If we were to accept that, why were you having a meeting with them then?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, according to this document, I was not the chief of the staff of the 306th Brigade. At that moment, I was the chief of staff of the Bosanska Krajina operations group. And the El Mujahid Detachment was resubordinated to the Bosanska Krajina operations group command for the purpose of carrying out this particular task. It was not Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond resubordinated to the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Could you for the benefit of the Trial Chamber tell us who exactly was in the El Mujahid Detachment? What was this detachment made up of, of who?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was never in the barracks, in the camp of that detachment. And I never visited the parts afield where the El Mujahid Detachment was involved in combat operations. But I do know that there were foreigners in the detachment, and there were some members of the local population who had agreed to abide by the code of conduct of that detachment or they had joined this formation for some other reasons. There were foreigners, mujahedin, and there were some local Bosniaks who had joined the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Hence the reason why you indicated to us on page 41 of the transcript, and correct me if I'm wrong, that it was a source of embarrassment. Isn't that the reason why, why they were a source of embarrassment, because they were included in the mujahedin detachment, were they, the mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was speaking about the period during which the El Mujahid Detachment hadn't been formed. Now, we have mostly been speaking about the period during which certain criminal acts were committed. We're not talking about the period during which the El Mujahid Detachment was formed, although there are numerous examples that when the El Mujahid Detachment was formed, there was maltreatment again, and the members of that detachment behaved inappropriately towards the civilian population, towards members of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, may the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P679, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could the document be placed on the ELMO so that we can see it and so that the accused can see it as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: My apologies, but the Defence was served a copy, so I thought...

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could you please turn to the second page. And do you see the signature of the commander?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed this document on behalf of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Well, that is even better because you're more familiar with it. So could we look at paragraph (c) on the first page. And this document was dated the 16th of March 1993. And shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I can assist you so that we can move on. "Frequent cases of all forms of crime in our zone of responsibility recently have damaged the combat readiness of units. And for that very reason, the security situation is visibly undermined. The Muslim units which are stationed in our zone of responsibility contribute to this significantly, but they are financed by people from Arab countries, so they have purchased plenty of MTS/technical equipment and materiels." And we can go on, but I think that is sufficient for you to explain to me and to the Trial Chamber what was really the relationship between the mujahedins, what role did they play? Could you help us?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, when the brigades were formed in the BH Republic Army, the men from the previous Muslim forces which wanted to join the army joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade of the BH Republic Army. But some of those Muslim forces didn't want to enter the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and they weren't part of the BH Republic Army. They were in contact with these people from Arab countries. And when they refer to the Muslim forces in a document of this kind, when they talk about being linked up with people from Arab countries, the reference being made is to the men who didn't join the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, or as I said, they're referring to men who were out of control and acting together with these foreigners. And in this document, we are providing information according to which this represents a problem in the zone of responsibility of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: It is your evidence, after you've looked at the report that you said was signed by you, and after you have looked at your worksheet that you drew up, that the mujahedins had absolutely no involvement at all in the 3rd Corps. That is your evidence as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, so far I have tried to avoid saying that while the El Mujahid Detachment existed and while the 3rd Corps existed, well, I try to avoid saying this. I meant -- I was referring to the period up to the formation of the El Mujahid Detachment. Up until that time, the mujahedin didn't participate together with the 306th Brigade in action, and they weren't resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. And I said that the first time they attempted to resubordinate them was unsuccessful. That was towards the ends of August, and they didn't succeed in doing this later on either. So I don't want to say that the El Mujahid Detachment was never -- I don't want to say that the El Mujahid Detachment was part of the BH Army or part of the corps. Because there were problems, and there were other problems because the 3rd Corps commander ordered that they be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. They refused this, and this shows how they carried out tasks. But as to the earlier period, this is the period I'm talking about, they never participated in combat action with the 306th Brigade and under the command of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And I am talking about the entire period relative to the period in the indictment. And I am talking about the fact that you have a document drafted by you in December referring to meetings with the El Mujahid Detachment. I'm talking about that. Now, I'm also going to ask you, in light of the fact that you told us there were foreigners in the El Mujahid Detachment as well, I'm going to ask you this: I take it that during your tenure that you had been to Mehurici before? During the conflict and before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: During the conflict, prior to the conflict, subsequent to the conflict, did you personally ever go to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Mehurici before the conflict and in the course of the conflict. From the 8th to the 15th, or perhaps the 20th, perhaps I didn't go to Mehurici, but I did go after the clashes, and naturally I did examine the situation in the units that were part of the 306th Brigade. But I never went to the camp where the mujahedin were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You said to me from the 8th to the 15th, or perhaps the 20th. Could you indicate perhaps what month that would have been?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June, when there was an open conflict in the Bila valley area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to ask you this question: The 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, do you know where they were based?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we had problems. We were involved in various tasks. I know that one battalion command was located in Travnik because I lived in Travnik, and I saw them there and had contact with them. But as to the location of the other battalions -- well, I also knew that a battalion command was -- brigade command, correction, was somewhere in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I am going to put this to you now. You have been to Mehurici before the conflict, after the conflict, and during. Do you know that the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was based in Mehurici in 1993?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in Mehurici, as far as I know, it was never located in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It's not an objection to my colleague's question. But in the transcript, I don't think it says that the battalion command was located in Zenica. I wanted to avoid any confusion. It's page 35, line 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: What about battalions of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade? Do you know if any such battalions were based in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. But the witness has just answered the question. He said that as far as he knew, there was no 7th Brigade battalion in Mehurici. And I'd like to Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond point out that the witness is the chief of the 306th Brigade, not of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, may the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 661, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Sir, does this order look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just let me have a look at it. I haven't seen this document before, but I remember the assistant commander for morale drafted this. He was from the 306th Brigade. And in one of the meetings of the brigade, he provided a briefing. This is why I remember this exchange with the 7th Muslim Brigade. I know that we also informed the superior command and the 7th Muslim Brigade. But I remember that we received an answer from the 7th Muslim Brigade, and they informed us in that answer that they had forwarded to their subordinate commands orders according to which such things should not occur. And according to their statements, according to their investigations, their members were not responsible for the acts in question. As to what happened to my wife later on in the same village referred to, it is obvious that on this occasion and on the second occasion, this was the responsibility or this act was committed by those who had joined the mujahedin in Mehurici. I can't recognise the document, but I remember all these events. I remember the letter from the 7th Muslim Brigade. And to a certain extent, I'm linking up these two events that have to do with the village of Kljaci, in April and in October. These acts were probably committed by members of the same unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: It would seem to me, and correct me if I'm wrong, that as chief of staff, you were sidelined most of the time. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I was sidelined as the chief of staff in relation to this document because this was drafted by the assistant commander for morale who was in direct connection with the brigade commander. It wasn't necessary for me. Maybe I didn't see the document, but I remember that at a meeting of the brigade command, this is a document that we discussed. This is something that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And do you remember discussing at one of those meetings the lawlessness and the outrageous behaviour of the mujahedins in your presence, in your area in particular?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was frequently discussed because the mujahedin caused problems to rise in our area. We informed our superior command of these criminal acts perpetrated by the mujahedin. We informed them of this because our combat readiness was being disturbed. It had an adverse effect on our combat readiness and on morale in the unit. Insecurity could be felt in the territory from which the 306th Brigade recruited men.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And you personally and your unit felt helpless, did you?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we weren't responsible for taking any measures. That wasn't our mandate. And I think that in such cases, since some of the Bosniak population had joined the mujahedin, as a result it was necessary to find some sort of a political solution. This problem should be resolved at a political level because for a commander to take the decision to deal with a given problem would involve having a lot of information, if he was to take the right decision. And on the basis of what we observed in the field, they had the support of some of the Bosniak people. We didn't know how many troops they had, and the politicians hadn't made us responsible for dealing with this problem. And perhaps this is why there was a feeling of helplessness as you have said.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And in addition to that, they, and correct me if I'm wrong because I'm only quoting from the order of the 16th of March 1993, these foreigners, as we call them, or mujahedins financed or these people from the Arab countries, they were able to finance the BiH and help the ABiH with respect to equipments and things like that in the early days. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this information, it was obtained by intelligence in the field. So that's the opinion of this intelligence officer providing the information. But I'm not in a position to come to such a conclusion. I wasn't so high ranking to be able to come to a conclusion as to how the army was financed or by whom. We relied on the legitimate bodies of power.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yet, they continued to embarrass you. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Even though the army had absolutely nothing to do with them, they continued to embarrass the army, they continued to be a source of concern to the army, an army that you said in evidence was larger than the HVO, an army that was bigger than them, and they couldn't do anything. Could you explain why? Why were they untouchable?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just tried to explain to you that we didn't have a mandate to enter into a conflict with them. This would have required a solution on the political level. We informed the authorities of the problems, but the 306th Brigade wasn't charged with entering a conflict with them. We didn't have such a mandate, and for the following reasons: As I said, they had the support of some of the population, some of the Bosniaks from the Bila valley, which is where they were located. In the villages, people started dividing mosques into two parts, and you would have religious rites of one kind in one part and of another in another part. The introduction of new norms of behaviour meant that it was necessary to deal with this issue at a higher level, and the 306th Brigade didn't have the authority to deal with this problem. It wasn't our responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: But according to you, they were in your area of responsibility at some point in time, one; you were the chief of staff, two; and you indicated a while ago that they were part of the El Mujahid Detachment, there were mujahedins in there. Now, to me, if they were part of the detachment and if they were in there, surely somebody had to have accepted them in there and had to have responsibility for them. And that's the reason why I come -- I agree with what you say when you said that they became a source of embarrassment. So can you tell me, how do we analyse this? Because in one breath, they weren't a part of the organisation. We had nothing to do with them. We didn't concern ourselves with them. For some reason, we turned a blind eye and we just stayed stiff where the mujahedins were concerned. We didn't want to have anything to do with them. In another breath, they were included in the detachment. Now, whoever was responsible for the mujahedin detachment had to be responsible for the members in it. Agreed? Agreed? So could you explain to me why --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my colleague is misquoting the witness who spoke about the mujahedin on a number of occasions up until late summer when they became the El Mujahid Detachment, and he spoke about the first time he had information about the detachment. According to my colleague's question, my colleague is putting words into the witness's mouth, saying something that the witness never said.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness was shown P679 as early as March 1993, and it talks about the mujahedins, and he said he was aware of the order of the mujahedins, and these people financing the army, people from the Arab countries. And it's just a simple question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I'm asking in light of all of this, what was the reason for the hands-off attitude towards the mujahedins? It's a simple question, and he can answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you understood the question? Do take your time before you answer it because it is an important question. So please, think about it and try to answer it if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To help you to understand this subject, it's necessary to start in 1992 before any kind of corps, any kind of brigades were formed, the mujahedin appeared. Foreigners appeared in the territory of the Travnik Municipality. This was before the establishment of units. It's not as if the commander of the 3rd Corps or the command of the 306th Brigade received them and billeted them there. Then, in the subsequent period, and as I said, the first time I heard about the El Mujahid's detachment was at the end of August when we received the order I mentioned. So this period, from the time they arrived right up until the end of August, during this period, they were these unofficial groups which caused problems. They weren't under army command. Because it's quite logical if the mujahedin imprisoned 30 inhabitants of Miletici, and if they were under the command of some army unit, in such a case, the command would have ordered them to release them. But what happened? People had to go and beg the mujahedin to release them. The father of a member of my command had to go there. If they had been within the system of command, they would have been given orders. From August and afterwards, they appeared in various areas. And there were units to which certain tasks were assigned. As to how they carried out the tasks, well, we have seen. And in this example, they refused to be resubordinated to the 306th Brigade. Later on, I came across the El Mujahid Detachment as a unit. This was in December when I moved into the Bosanska Krajina OG and when I had to perform the duties of chief of staff. And this is when I received a task to draft a plan to assist the population that was under threat in Old Vitez, in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I don't intend to continue much further with this, but I would want to ask you this, and I think you keep missing the question. And the question is just this: Why were they hesitant in disciplining them, whether they came in after in the mujahedin unit or before? Why was there that hesitancy in disciplining this group of people, a small group of people that was much smaller than the army, a group of people that was terrorising everybody? And here with an army, a force of - you told us how much your unit alone had - 5.000, whatever. Why is it that nobody saw it fit to discipline this unit or this body of people, more so when they became embodied into the Mujahid unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, take your time before you reply. The question that has been put to you is attached to an incident that concerned you because it involved your wife. Your wife who was a teacher was forced to leave the village where she was teaching school because of the mujahedin. And the Prosecution now asks you to explain how come that a situation like that could occur, and there were other witnesses who testified to that. And how come that the 3rd Corps, somebody even mentioned that the 3rd Corps had 30.000 troops. You, in your zone of responsibility, there is a document saying that there were about 11.000 of you. At the moment, when you were there, there were 5.000 troops. How can you explain the fact that 5.000 soldiers could be terrorised by a dozen or so individuals? And this is what the Prosecution has just asked you. Try to respond, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I have been talking about the mujahedin, I have tried to explain on several occasions what this was all about. I don't know whether I have to go over the same ground again. In a nutshell, let me repeat. I don't know what else to say. Some of the local population joined the mujahedin for various reasons. So they enjoyed their support. The conflict or the solution to these problems would have led up to terrible consequences, and the commander of the 306th Brigade could not make such decisions. He would have had to have all the relevant data on the possible consequences of this possible conflict. This surpassed his means. And since these people enjoyed the support of some of the civilian population, he would have had to have had political consent to deal with this situation. And this went beyond me or beyond the brigade commander. When I was talking about the strength of the army in that area, I was talking about the number of troops. And I said that at the moment when the conflict began, the number of men did not correspond to the number of weapons, only 50 per cent of the troops had arms, were armed. I was talking about the strength when I was responding to a question. And I said that the technical capabilities of the HVO when the Frankopan Brigade was established, the balance of forces was changed in their favour significantly. And if you will allow me one more thing, when we're talking about the incident that happened in October, I know, because my wife was involved, I'm familiar with the case, this person who was a member of the El Mujahid Detachment, he was tried and sentenced or punished. I don't know how he was punished. However, I know that he had to appear before the court in Travnik for this incident that took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Siljak. Would you be able to assist us with the name of that person, that mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a local Muslim whose name was Sabahudin Adilovic. He was born in Kljaci village, in my village where I was born. And he was the one who forced my wife out of the village. And she only wanted to teach the kids there to write and read in those times of adversity. He was not a mujahedin, but he joined the group of mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And this would be my last question on that topic: With respect to combat activities, could you -- would you be able to assist the Trial Chamber as to the role the mujahedins played with respect to combat activities. Perhaps you could enlighten us as to who they were fighting against, you know.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak about the planned activities in December when I was the chief of staff of the Bosanska Krajina OG. At that time, the El Mujahid Detachment like all the other units was assigned certain tasks within the overall mission of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: As to the middle of 1993, do you know what they were doing, what was their role?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In mid-1993, they were informal groups. We did not have any information as to how they carried out combat activities or what they did. Their camp, as I've already said, was in Poljanica. Their camp was very close to the sector where combat activities took place. And most often, they would get involved in plundering. When the BiH Army units liberated an area, they would come in to take the loot, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And I take it that the BiH Army was helpless? They couldn't stop them from looting, could they?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 306th Brigade at the time had the main task to reach Bukovica as soon as possible, to reach Bandol as soon as possible because Bandol had come under attack. After the BH Army, and I'm sure that everybody from that area can confirm that, there were civilians, there were mujahedins, everybody started looting, people were hungry. There were a lot of refugees. We were engaged in combat activities. Or at least according to my information, we were engaged in combat on this axis that led to Bukovica, and we tried to get there as soon as possible. We didn't have much time for anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd just like to go into the areas that my learned friend dealt with with respect to the crimes committed in Miletici and Maline. And in your evidence in chief, you indicated that most of it you said you weren't aware about; the information you had is what was relayed to you. So in light of that, my question to you is this: On learning what had happened in these different areas that you said you personally wasn't aware of, did you inform your superior, and could you tell us what action was taken, if any?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
